scope: Apply BROC practice, Star selection and historical-publication continuity migrations; deploy the compatible existing application; verify privacy and public continuity without activating or generating Star work.
findings: The forward migration preserves only pre-cutover completed Star works whose autonomous identity, actor, discoverable active profile, attempt, generation, request, stored asset, timestamps and existing publication state agree. It excludes work with a BROC candidate or selection event.

The archive ledger is append-only, forced-RLS, and inaccessible to anon, authenticated and service_role. New Star request admission still requires actor activation. Activation no longer hides established work or blocks review of a completed candidate.
Selection remains a separate internal decision. The production selection command was not run and no new Star candidate was generated or selected.
Existing application surfaces and navigation were retained. No new application, dashboard, route shell, publishing path or public prompt surface was added.
Public feed readback returned 11 unique Star works. The response used the explicit public DTO, contained no prompt field, and returned no human works.
The existing Premium relay queue was not changed by this rollout; its current R4 deployment remains documented in its separate private release record.

production_changes: Applied the three BROC/Star migrations to the existing linked application database and deployed the compatible existing GALX application. No Star activation, generation, candidate selection, allowance change, queue mutation or new Docker build was performed.
known_findings: The linked database advisor still reports one existing SECURITY DEFINER view on public.community_participant_profiles. It remains the curated participant projection with its existing explicit output and grants; this rollout did not redesign that permission model. Track a separate focused review before changing it.
The internal candidate-review command was not executed against production; selection and withholding were tested in disposable PostgreSQL only.
limits: The live feed verifies publication continuity and the prompt-free response shape; it is not a review or selection of any new work.
The release did not perform provider inference, enable a Star, change purchased allowances, or test account-specific private generation.
The production public-boundary scan covered the listed routes and 37 browser assets, not every possible third-party cache or previously downloaded copy.
No new queue runtime was built because the relay queue source and deployed image were unchanged in this migration/application rollout.
